subject: English
central_question: How can a student choose and combine tense forms accurately when events occur at different times or appear in future time clauses and reported conditionals?
in_scope_units: Mixed-tense sentences that describe two related events occurring at different times
Future time clauses with when, while, as soon as, until, before, and after
Simple present for definite future schedules and arrangements
banned_topics: Complete rules of active and passive voice
Subject-verb concord rules unrelated to tense choice

known_pitfalls.claim: A future time clause must use will because it refers to the future.
known_pitfalls.correction: After when, while, as soon as, until, before, and after, use the simple present for future meaning; keep will in the main clause.

known_pitfalls.claim: Both events in a sentence must always use the same tense.
known_pitfalls.correction: Related events may correctly use different tenses when their time relationship is different, such as simple present in a time clause with future perfect in the main clause.

known_pitfalls.claim: In reported conditionals, only the main clause changes tense.
known_pitfalls.correction: When the reporting verb creates a past-time frame, both the if-clause and the main clause shift consistently, for example study/will becomes studied/would.

recommended_example_progression: Fill in a blank using future perfect with a simple-present time clause
Correct the use of will inside a future time clause
Rewrite a direct conditional statement in reported speech
Complete a timetable sentence using the simple present
Correct a mixed-tense sequencing error using the past perfect
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Typical CBSE practice uses gap filling, sentence completion, dialogue reporting, and error correction in mixed-tense contexts.
